model_annotation:
This figure contains two subplots, labeled (a) and (b), which together show training loss curves for training from scratch using different methods.

**Plot (a): Loss w.r.t steps.** This plot illustrates the training loss as a function of training steps for several model configurations. The x-axis represents training steps, displayed on a linear scale ranging from approximately 0 to 140,000 (with tick marks at regular intervals). The y-axis represents the loss value, on a linear scale ranging from approximately 3.0 to 5.5. Five lines are shown. The dark red line, labeled "Vanilla," starts at approximately 5.3 at step 0 and decreases steeply before leveling off to around 3.2 by 140,000 steps. The green line, labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)," follows a very similar trajectory to Vanilla, starting near 5.3 and declining to approximately 3.2. The blue line, labeled "SepLLM (n=64)," starts similarly near 5.3 and decreases to roughly 3.15–3.2 by the end, tracking closely with the Vanilla and StrmLLM curves. The orange line, labeled "SepLLM (n=128)," also starts near 5.3 and decreases to approximately 3.15 by 140,000 steps, appearing slightly below the previous curves in the later portion. The purple line, labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)," starts near 5.3 and decreases to approximately 3.1 by 140,000 steps, consistently sitting at or slightly below the other curves in the latter half of training.

**Plot (b): Loss Ratio w.r.t FLOPs.** This plot shows the ratios of the loss values of different methods to that of Vanilla with respect to FLOPs. The x-axis represents FLOPs, displayed on a linear scale (with values appearing to range from approximately 0 to a maximum value, with tick labels visible). The y-axis represents the loss ratio, ranging from approximately 0.97 to 1.03. Four lines are shown, corresponding to StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The green line (StrmLLM, n=64) starts above 1.0 at low FLOPs and generally remains near or slightly above 1.0 throughout, indicating a loss ratio close to Vanilla. The blue line (SepLLM, n=64) begins above 1.0 and decreases, settling near or slightly below 1.0. The orange line (SepLLM, n=128) follows a similar pattern, decreasing from above 1.0 to values slightly below 1.0. The purple line (SepLLM, n=64, H/T) starts above 1.0 and decreases to values consistently below 1.0 in the later portion, reaching approximately 0.97–0.98 by the end, representing the lowest loss ratio among the methods shown.
